networkPolicy.desc: Its station data, the map tiles and its Firebase sign in, and nothing else

notes:
An allow list, written from the binary. It is a Flutter application, so its own code is in lib/arm64-v8a/libapp.so in the ABI split, which tools/extract_hosts.py does not read; the strings there were read by hand.

What it dials: docs.google.com, where the station list is a Google Sheet (gviz/tq?tqx=out:json) and reports go to two Google Forms (formResponse); tile.openstreetmap.org for the map; Firestore, and Firebase Auth with Google sign in and reCAPTCHA (identitytoolkit, securetoken, firebaseinstallations, www.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com, www.recaptcha.net, www.gstatic.com/recaptcha). www.google.com is asked for its favicon, which reads as a connectivity check.

Not dialled: waze.com/ul and google.com/maps/dir are links handed to the navigation apps. The base APK also carries dozens of github.com hosts and YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, LinkedIn and X: library resources, never used. No ads, no analytics, no Crashlytics were found.

Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel: a host built at runtime would show up there as WHITELIST_MISS.
